inconsistencies: Rebroadcast privacy is attacked by five overlapping PRs: #36398 (only rebroadcast own txs), #36482 (only announce if re-added to mempool), #36330 (don't resubmit under -privatebroadcast), #34533 (resubmit *through* private broadcast), #36380 (-walletbroadcast=initialonly). #34533 and #36330 are directly contradictory for the same configuration; an approach decision is needed before either is reviewed in depth. #36398 is the broadest fix and should be reviewed first.

Dependency chain that must be reviewed in order: #33033 (SQLite statement RAII) -> #33034 (transactions in their own table) -> #27865 (no-longer-spendable TXO tracking). #27865's benchmarked speedup is the payoff for the whole chain, which is why the two bases were raised to its band.

Dependency chain: #36442 (multipath descriptor object) -> #36443 (reconstruct multipath) -> #36444 (store multipath info in wallet). #36443 was raised because it cannot sit below #36444, which needs it.
Dependency chain: #10102 (multiprocess) -> #19460 (bitcoin-wallet -ipcconnect) -> #19461. #19460 has no standalone wallet benefit until #10102 lands.

#35918 (expose key expression parsing), #36070 (deriveHDKey interface) and #36143 (CreateMultisigDescriptor) are three separate prerequisites for the same GUI multisig wizard (#35645); they should be scheduled together so the wizard is not blocked on the slowest one.
#36494 and #36344 both harden sendall argument handling and touch the same RPC option path; review #36494 first (unknown-option rejection is the broader footgun) and rebase #36344 on it.
#36339 and #36342 both fix bitcoind crashes triggered by out-of-range numeric arguments to wallet RPCs; they were in different bands and are now aligned.
#35742 and #36420 both fix the Miniscript/descriptor duplicate-key sanity check (different branches of the same logic); reviewing them together avoids conflicting fixes to the same function.
#30343 removes WalletLogPrintf entirely while #36397 is a scripted diff normalising WalletLogPrintf call sites; #36397 becomes largely moot if #30343 lands, so decide the order explicitly.
#36114 states it absorbs and supersedes #35358; reviewers should not spend time on the superseded approach.
#32966 (receiving) and #35302 (sending) are halves of one silent payments project and are also gated on upstream libsecp256k1 work; receiving should be reviewed first.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: a small P1 set covering fund diversion, database-write corruption, load-time crashes, silent rescan omissions and migration corruption; a large P2 band of concrete bugs, privacy leaks, measured speedups and the multi-PR descriptor/storage/silent-payments projects; then a long P3 tail of deferrable fixes, features and refactors. Several bands were adjusted only to keep dependency chains from inverting (#33033, #36443) or to align PRs with identical consequences (#36342 with #36339, #34533 with the rest of the rebroadcast cluster).
